hero.headingHtml:
Research that builds
pathways to equity
in STEM education.
hero.description: Dr. Mo. Lab advances equitable and inclusive engineering education through research that responds to the needs of diverse students, educators, and communities. We explore how culture, context, and access shape opportunities to learn, teach, and participate in STEM, developing approaches that are culturally relevant, globally informed, and grounded in the communities they serve.

acronym.bodyHtml: DRMO Lab is a research group dedicated to developing researchers and advancing multidisciplinary approaches to engineering education and outreach. We work across disciplines, institutions, and communities to create research that is responsive to real-world needs while expanding opportunities for students and researchers to engage in meaningful scholarship. Through collaboration and outreach, we seek to connect research with the people and communities it is meant to serve.

pi.name: Dr. Moses Olayemi
pi.title: Assistant Professor of Engineering Pathways · Gallogly College of Engineering · University of Oklahoma
pi.bio: Dr. Moses Olayemi (Dr. Mo) is a scholar at the intersection of STEM education, culturally relevant pedagogy, and socioeconomic development. Originally from Nigeria, he holds a B.Sc. in Chemical Engineering from the University of Lagos and a Ph.D. in Engineering Education from Purdue University, where he was awarded the Bilsland Dissertation Fellowship. His work has been recognized internationally — his paper on culturally relevant engineering education in Nigeria won the ASEE International Division's Best DEI Paper in 2023. At OU, he teaches Introduction to Engineering Thinking and is known as one of the college's most student-centered instructors.
